metadata.note: The Winona and St. Peter Railroad reached Rochester, MN on Oct 12 1864 -- the city's first railroad, well before the Mayo Clinic existed (founded 1889) -- and was later absorbed into the Chicago and North Western. Rochester grew into a branch hub (lines also radiated to Zumbrota, Plainview, and Chatfield, not traced here), but this Winona-Rochester segment was the original main stem and the one that mattered most once the Mayo Clinic became a national draw: from the 1930s, the C&NW ran dedicated hospital cars (the 'Lister', built 1930, with wide doors for stretcher patients) on the streamlined Rochester 400, carrying Mayo-bound patients from Chicago until the train's final run Jul 23 1963. Geometry traced through real track using OpenStreetMap data (Overpass API) and shortest-path graph search; traced length (50.7 mi) is a plausible match for this branch.
metadata.source: postbulletin.com (Even 100 years ago... / Patients heading to Mayo Clinic rode in comfort on the Lister), winonadailynews.com (A city of rails), Wikipedia (Winona and St. Peter Railroad), american-rails.com (Minnesota '400')
